findings.detail: TxQ orders by fee level descending, ties by (txID XOR parentHash) ascending (R-01). Two validators with different parent hashes order the same equal-fee queue differently; consensus agrees the tx set, never the queue order (R-36).
findings.title: Same-fee queue order is parent-hash-salted, so queue order is local, never consensus-agreed

findings.detail: ValidatorList.cpp:1898-1900 states a 67% quorum for devnet/testnet with a comment that mainnet should revert to 80% (R-28). Any simulator or safety argument assuming 80% is wrong for this codebase; the fork-safety margin depends on UNL overlap per the cited theorem (arXiv:1802.07242).
findings.title: This fork validates at a 67% quorum, not upstream XRPL's 80%

findings.detail: Preclaim fails with tefMAX_LEDGER only when view.seq() > LastLedgerSequence (R-14), so a transaction may still be included in the ledger whose seq equals its LLS; queued transactions with LLS <= closed ledger seq are evicted (R-13). The off-by-one is in the ledger index compared (open seq vs closed seq); a simulator using one comparison for both is wrong. S-04 reproduces both boundaries.
findings.title: LastLedgerSequence is inclusive at preclaim but eviction uses <= at close — the same boundary value means different things

findings.detail: scaleFeeLevel returns multiplier x current^2 / target^2 once the open ledger passes txnsExpected (R-03, TxQ.cpp:173-195). A simulator using exponential growth over-prices spikes.
findings.title: Fee escalation is quadratic in code, not exponential as docs say

findings.detail: ConsensusParms.h avalancheCutoffs: init 50%, mid 65%, late 70%, stuck 95% (R-18). Code wins; docs are stale on this point.
findings.title: The dispute avalanche ladder in code is 50/65/70/95, not the 50/60/... quoted in some XRPL docs

findings.detail: A new transaction is admitted to a full queue only if its fee beats the average fee of the cheapest account's queued transactions, and the victim is that account's last (highest-sequence) transaction (R-31). A cheap transaction can survive inside a high-average account while a mid-fee transaction elsewhere is evicted. S-05 models this.
findings.title: Queue-full eviction is per-account-average, not global-lowest-fee

findings.detail: TxQ.cpp:913 uses a strict `feeLevelPaid > requiredRetryLevel` comparison (R-11). S-02 shows the exact-25% case (512 -> 640) rejected while 512 -> 665 succeeds.
findings.title: Replacement requires STRICTLY more than +25%; exactly +25% is rejected

findings.detail: Submitting two payloads at one sequence costs nothing beyond the fee of the one that applies: the first to apply wins, later ones get tefPAST_SEQ, and the queue treats the second as a replacement candidate (R-24). No slashing, no account flag.
findings.title: No equivocation penalty exists

findings.detail: Proposed-but-unaccepted transactions are tracked and warned every 15 ledgers; detection never forces inclusion or reorders anything (R-33). A transaction can be delayed indefinitely by repeated NO votes with no in-protocol remedy.
findings.title: Censorship detection only warns every 15 ledgers

findings.detail: Blocker transactions (SetRegularKey, SignerListSet, etc.) must be alone in an account's queue: a blocker is rejected if the account already has queued transactions, and no further transaction may queue behind one (R-25).
findings.title: Blocker transactions serialise an account's queue

findings.detail: Fee escalation can no longer be toggled off by amendment vote in this build; its behaviour is unconditional (R-30).
findings.title: FeeEscalation is a retired amendment

findings.detail: Locally-submitted transactions are re-applied to new open ledgers for up to 5 ledgers (holdLedgers, R-26). A locally-submitted transaction lost in a fork longer than 5 ledgers is silently dropped from re-proposal.
findings.title: Local-transaction re-proposal lasts only 5 ledgers
